answer: A quadratic attestation price stops bulk identity farming. Each identity needs priced attestations, and the k-th attestation bought by one operator costs k squared credits, so one history cannot be shared across clones. A raven auditor checks that each pulse of work belongs to a single key; reuse is rejected and the bond slashed. The named failure is attestation laundering: clones hidden in karst pockets still pay the quadratic price, so 1,000 fakes needing ten attestations each cost 385,000 credits, while an honest agent pays only the first, cheapest one.
